_doc: Coverage as data (Fendi, 2026-10-02): music videos are built from camera movement and angle changes; a static single-angle performance shot is the rare exception. For every performance line the tool buys COVERAGE the way a low-budget shoot does — several passes of the same performance from different cameras — from one real take: (1) camera moves on the real take (scripts/edit/camera_coverage.py, $0, pixel-true, lip-locked; 2.5D via camera_engine.py when a matte export exists, 2D otherwise), (2) new angles from the same take (Seedance 2.5 reference-to-video, ~$4 per angle, lip motion close not locked → cutaways between on-mic lines), (3) cuts between them on the beat grid with angle rotation. Sections come from lyric_lines (verse/hook/bridge/adlib) or the shot's section field; 'default' covers the rest. Move odds are relative weights; the planner draws deterministically (seeded by shot id) and applies the rotation rules. Amounts are fractions of the frame (push 0.18 = 18 % tighter by the end). Lens names are scripts/edit/lens_presets.json. Whip pans live in the TRANSITIONS (config/transition_presets.json), not in the move vocabulary: a whip as an in-shot move on a one-bar cut arrives from off-frame and shows the frame edge (measured on bar3, 2026-10-02); as a transition it straddles the cut and never does.

angle_gate._doc: A generated angle re-draws the performer. It is cut onto a sung line only when its fidelity report (scripts/qa/reference_fidelity.py → <angle>_fidelity.json) shows the face is still his and the mouth follows the take; the lip fit also sets where the angle sits on the take's clock.
